title: Compress PDF to 250 KB Online: Free 250 KB PDF, Private
description: Compress a PDF to 250 KB with every page redrawn on your own device. Good for 4–7 page scans and forms with a 250 KB cap. Free, no sign-up, never uploaded.
intro: Get a 250 KB PDF from a scan that is too large for your form. The compressor redraws the pages on your device and keeps the highest quality that fits under 250 KB.

steps.name: Load the document
steps.text: Pick the PDF that the portal rejected for being too large.

steps.name: Use the 250 KB target
steps.text: It is preselected; other common limits sit beside it.

steps.name: Compress
steps.text: Long files are sampled first, so a 20-page scan does not take a full pass at every resolution.

steps.name: Verify
steps.text: Scroll through the preview and download once the size is ticked.

faq.q: Can I compress a 20-page PDF to 250 KB?
faq.a: Not with readable text. Even at 72 DPI twenty pages need far more. Upload only the pages asked for.

faq.q: Why does a long PDF take a while?
faq.a: Every page has to be drawn and re-encoded on your device. A phone handles a few pages per second.

faq.q: Will the PDF stay under 250 KB on the portal?
faq.a: Yes. It is kept below 250,000 bytes, so it passes whether the portal divides by 1000 or 1024.

faq.q: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The PDF is opened, redrawn and saved inside your browser. It never leaves your device, and the page keeps working offline after your first visit.

sections.h2: When 250 KB is the right target
paras: A 250 KB limit is not common in the exam notices we track; you will meet it mainly on admission and scholarship portals. It is still a useful safety target for NTA uploads when the scan has several pages. CUET UG and UGC NET both want the disability (UDID) certificate as a PDF of 50 to 300 KB, and a 250 KB file leaves a margin below the ceiling without throwing away detail you might need.

sections.h2: How many pages fit in 250 KB
paras: Four to seven scanned pages at 72 or 100 DPI, or about two at 150 DPI. A clean, evenly lit page costs much less than a dim one with a grey cast, so the same certificate can fit five pages or eight depending on how it was photographed. Beyond about ten pages, 250 KB is out of reach.

Scan every page in the same light and at the same distance; one dark page drags the quality of all the others down, because the whole PDF shares one size budget. For text PDFs with embedded fonts, a size over 250 KB usually comes from a large logo or scanned signature inside. The tool asks before rasterising such a file, since its text would become an image.
Your form has a different limit? Open that size, or the PDF resize hub to type any number. Starting from photos instead of a PDF? Making the PDF from the photos gives sharper pages.
